parole.testo: From Ewe avuvi (“puppy”), from avu (“dog”) + the diminutive suffix -vi, which may be related to vi (“little; child”); or the equivalent in another Gbe language.

parole.significato: An ethnic group who inhabit southeastern Ghana, Togo, and Benin.
A member of a Yoruba people living in coastal regions of modern-day Benin and Nigeria, especially one taken to the Cari…
parole.testo: From Ewe Anagó (“a Yoruba”), from Yoruba Ànàgó (“Yoruba from Abeokuta Province, Nigeria”).

parole.significato: The practice of ritual servitude in parts of Africa.
parole.testo: From the Ewe words tro (“god”) + kosi (“female slave”).
